page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m8-vws.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.vgn6i-vws family. It is equipped with 10 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 46.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 4.6 GB of memory per core. For graphics and parallel computing acceleration, the instance includes a fractional NVIDIA T4 GPU, delivering 8 GB of VRAM. It does not include local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. However, multi-core performance is more robust, achieving average ratings in stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth also performs at an average level, reaching 48.09 GB/sec for large block reads. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates average performance in image processing, ray tracing, and software compilation, but struggles with single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing.

The inclusion of a fractional NVIDIA T4 GPU makes this instance suitable for entry-level GPU-accelerated tasks. While it handles LLM inference for small 135M models at an average speed of 130.14 tokens/sec for text generation, performance drops significantly to a poor rating for medium 7B models. Consequently, this server is best suited for virtual workstations, moderate image processing, ray tracing, and lightweight machine learning inference rather than heavy LLM workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the fractional GPU allocation allows users to access hardware acceleration without paying for a full GPU, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that do not saturate a complete graphics card.
